sources.entry: AeroSpace - i3-like tiling window manager for macOS. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/nikitabobko/AeroSpace) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: AeroSpace is an i3-like tiling window manager for macOS that uses its own emulated virtual workspaces and does not require disabling SIP.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a tiling window manager built on a tree layout model and inspired by i3. Workspace switching is done by AeroSpace's own virtual workspace emulation rather than native macOS Spaces, and switching is stated to be fast and free of animations. Configuration is a plain text file (a default-config.toml is referenced), and the tool is described as CLI-first with manpages and shell completion included. Multi-monitor support follows an i3-like paradigm, and the README asks users to arrange monitors properly in multi-monitor setups. The README also states that the project uses one private API (_AXUIElementGetWindow) and otherwise relies on public accessibility APIs.
use_cases: tile windows automatically on a mac
scripted window control from the command line
notable: Emulates its own virtual workspaces instead of using macOS Spaces, and does not require disabling SIP
Plain text TOML configuration, positioned as dotfiles friendly
CLI-first design with manpages and shell completion
Homebrew install provides autoupdates; README notes the app is not notarized and the Homebrew script removes the quarantine attribute
Shell-like combinators (||, &&, ;) and an eval command for sending multiple commands
caveats: Public Beta: the README says to expect breaking changes until 1.0 is reached
Not notarized by Apple; the README acknowledges this as a known trait of the distribution
Release builds from source require macOS 15+ with Swift 6.4 and Xcode 26.6+; the binary runs on macOS 13+
